title: Service Bus Sessions and Ordered Message Processing
description: Use sessions to guarantee ordered processing of related messages by the same receiver.

data.text: A session is a grouping mechanism for messages. When messages share the same session ID, Service Bus delivers them to the same receiver in order. This is useful for workflows where messages must be processed sequentially, such as an order that has multiple steps (authorize, charge, ship).

terms.definition: A user-defined property that groups related messages together.
An exclusive lock on a session so only one receiver processes it at a time.
The number of sessions that can be processed simultaneously by the same receiver.
Optional per-session state stored by Service Bus for the duration of the session.

data.title: Session Best Practice
data.text: Set maxConcurrentSessions based on your receiver capacity. Too low and you waste throughput; too high and you risk overwhelming downstream systems.
